name: Blood glucose (home meter)
rangeNote: Fasting (nothing to eat for 8 hours): 3.9–5.5 mmol/L (70–99 mg/dL); 5.6–6.9 is called impaired fasting glucose. About 2 hours after a meal: below 7.8 mmol/L (140 mg/dL). At any time, 11.1 (200) or more with symptoms such as thirst and passing a lot of urine needs a doctor. Below 3.0 (54) is a significant low. Home meters can be about 15 % off, and a diagnosis needs a lab test.
summary: The sugar level in your blood right now, from a finger-prick meter or a sensor. It moves through the day with meals, activity, stress and sleep, so the time of day and whether you'd eaten matter for reading it.

high.meaning: A high fasting reading, or high readings long after meals, can be an early sign of prediabetes or diabetes. One reading isn't a diagnosis: a lab test (fasting glucose or HbA1c) is.
commonCauses: A recent meal or sugary drink

low.meaning: Low blood sugar can cause shakiness, sweating, confusion or fainting. In people without diabetes medicines it is uncommon; repeated lows are worth discussing with a doctor.
commonCauses: Diabetes medicines such as insulin or sulfonylureas
